cur:objects-ratchis-altar.summary: On the front of this Lombard altar Christ sits frontally within a mandorla carried by four flying angels, holding a book and blessing, while cherubim appear beside him. The flat, linear carving and the large heads and hands of the figures are typical of Lombard sculpture. The sides show the Visitation and the Adoration of the Magi, so that the altar unites the Incarnation with the glory of Christ.
facts: The altar is dated 737–744, while Ratchis, son of Duke Pemmo, ruled Friuli before becoming king of the Lombards in 744 (Wikipedia; museum dating recorded with the photographs).
The relief was originally painted; the museum presents a multimedia reconstruction of its original colours.
